points.quote: The workbench is the window manager for the app. It owns the main area (one or more side-by-side views) and the right sidebar.
`View` (`entities/view.ts`) is one managed window. ... `Workbench` ... holds `views$`, `activeViewIndex$` and `activeView$`. ... `SplitView` lays the views out side by side.
It has its own history (`createNavigableHistory`), plus `location$`, `entries$`, ... `push`, `replace`, `go`
`ViewRoot` creates a private `createMemoryRouter(routes)` for each view. A layout effect calls `viewRouter.navigate(location)` whenever the view's `location$` changes.

A route component declares `<ViewHeader>`, `<ViewBody>` and `<ViewSidebarTab>`. These are the Provider halves of the "islands" in `view-islands.tsx`. They portal their content into the matching Targets.
Exactly one view is active. The active view's URL is treated as the URL of the whole app.
`WorkbenchSidebar` shows only the active view's sidebar, with a switcher when the view has several tabs.
`browser-adapter.ts` binds the active view to the browser router ... a browser location change ... the view calls `history.go(delta)`. That is how browser back/forward moves the view.
